question: The bat swarms in Batman Returns were never animated bat by bat. So who decided where each bat flew?
answer: The other bats. In 1987 Craig Reynolds published Boids, a program in which each simulated bird sees only its nearby flockmates and obeys three rules: don't crowd them, head where they head, stay near them. Lifelike flocks appear with no one steering. Batman Returns (1992) used the idea for its bats and its marching penguins.
move: Before scripting a crowd, find the rule each member follows.
ask: Which group I belong to is steered by a few rules nobody says aloud?

scene.caption: Three rules for every bird: don't crowd, head where your neighbours head, stay near.
scene.reveal: Nobody scripted that split. It came out of the three rules, as it does every time.

reference: Reynolds, Flocks, herds and schools: a distributed behavioral model, Computer Graphics 21(4):25-34 (SIGGRAPH 1987); https://www.red3d.com/cwr/boids/
